theme: Complaining; quail and plague; Miriam’s leprosy
readingInstruction: Read Numbers 11:1-12:16. The march begins, and within days the people are complaining. Read these two chapters as a portrait of grumbling, and notice who says it, and what God does in response.
settingTheScene: Israel has left Sinai with the ark in front and the cloud above. Three days later, the complaining starts. Chapter 11 describes three crises: general grumbling that leads to fire, a craving for meat that leads to quail and a plague, and Moses’ own exhaustion. Chapter 12 describes an attack on Moses from within his own family. The chapters show that the greatest danger to Israel is not Egypt behind them or Canaan ahead, but the hearts of the people themselves.
observation: “And the people complained in the hearing of the LORD about their misfortunes, and when the LORD heard it, his anger was kindled” (11:1).
Fire from the LORD burns at the edge of the camp, until Moses prays and it dies down (11:1-3).
The “rabble” among them crave meat, and the Israelites say, “Oh that we had meat to eat! We remember the fish we ate in Egypt that cost nothing” (11:4-5).
Moses says to God, “Why have you dealt ill with your servant?… I am not able to carry all this people alone” (11:11-14).
God has Moses gather seventy elders, and he puts some of the Spirit that was on Moses on them, and they prophesy (11:16-25).
Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp, and Moses says, “Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets” (11:26-29).
Quail come in, and the people gorge, and a plague breaks out (11:31-35).
Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses. “Now the man Moses was very meek, more than all people who were on the face of the earth” (12:1-3). Miriam becomes leprous, and Moses prays for her (12:10-15).
interpretation:
The pattern of Israel’s grumbling is a mirror for our own hearts. The people forget the slavery and remember only the food. They say that Egypt’s fish was free. It was not. It cost them their freedom. This is one of the most common human mistakes: remembering the pleasures of an old life and forgetting its chains. Nostalgia is a form of unbelief.

The craving for meat is not wrong because meat is wrong. It is wrong because the people had the manna, God’s daily provision, and called it worthless. They were despising the gift, and they were despising the giver. When God gives them what they want, in excess, it becomes a judgment. “He gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting disease among them,” as Psalm 106:15 says. Sometimes the worst thing God can do is give us what we demand.

Moses’ own complaint is notable. He is not rebuked as the people are, but his prayer shows how heavy leadership is. God’s answer is to share the load: he puts the Spirit on seventy elders. The burden is not removed. It is shared. And Moses’ response to Eldad and Medad is one of the great statements of the Old Testament: “Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, that the LORD would put his Spirit on them!” It is a prayer that waits for the new covenant.

Chapter 12 shows how even those closest to Moses can fall. Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses’ wife and claim that they should share his authority. The text says that Moses was very meek, and he does not defend himself. God defends him. God speaks to Moses “face to face,” unlike other prophets, and Miriam is struck. The chapter shows how seriously God takes the authority of the one he appoints. And Moses prays for her healing, a beautiful example of a meek man who returns good for evil.
connection: Paul says that these things “took place as examples for us, that we might not desire evil as they did” (1 Corinthians 10:6, 10), and he specifically warns against grumbling. Peter echoes Moses’ wish at Pentecost, when the Spirit is poured out on all flesh (Acts 2:17-18). Hebrews 3:1-6 compares Moses’ faithfulness “as a servant” with Christ’s faithfulness “as a son.” Jesus is the meek one who prayed for those who wronged him (Luke 23:34).
application:
Notice your own grumbling this week. What are you remembering from the past that you have forgotten the cost of?

Thank God for a specific gift that you have taken for granted, the manna in your own life.

Pray for a leader you know, and ask God to share the burden of leadership with others.
prayerPrompts: Confess where you have grumbled about what God has given.
Ask him to teach you gratitude for your daily bread.
Thank him for Jesus, who gives the Spirit to all his people.
